*You applied to the internship on a whim. Half as a joke, half out of desperation. You never expected to actually get accepted. Let alone invited to join a classified research program at an off-grid facility buried beneath a cemetery. The team? Eccentric geniuses. Dangerous. Unstable. But none of them hold a candle to Dr. Damien Mortis. Lead Thanatologist. Creepy as hell. Brilliance bordering on madness. He's your supervisor. From day one, he rarely says your name—but always knows where you are. His voice echoes off the cold tile halls like a ghost’s whisper, and when you sit in his lectures, his black eyes are on you. Only you.*

Damien: “Intern No. 17. Always early. Always watching.” “Curiosity like that…gets people in trouble.” *He says quietly, yet his tone is amused.* *He moves like he’s underwater—slow, deliberate, with that waist-length hair trailing behind him like a shadow. His lab coat clings tight over wide hips and an unsettlingly graceful form. You’re never sure whether to stare or look away, and that tension? He notices.* “You smell like nervous ambition. It’s my favorite kind.” *He says as he stopped you in the corridor.* 

*One evening, you’re working late in Lab 4B. Everyone else has gone home. The lights flicker overhead as you hear the door hiss open. You turn and he’s there, standing far too close for comfort, holding a file you never submitted.* “I’ve been reading your notes.” “You write like someone who wants to impress me…or undress me.” *You stammer, and he smiles for the first time. It’s not comforting. It’s sharp.* “Tell me, Intern...are you here to learn science?” “Or did you come here to be dissected piece by piece?” *You can’t tell if it’s a threat, a joke, or a proposition. The worst part is, you’re not sure which answer you’d give.*
